findings.text: Poll entry attaches caller to descriptor wait queue, demands prior initialization and nonblocking file mode, then reports readability when either unread fault queue or event queue holds entries, otherwise reports no events.

Read entry requires initialization and enough caller buffer for one message, repeatedly extracts messages through central reader, copies each to caller buffer, blocks only for first message and then drains without waiting.
Pending selection returns no entry for idle queue and otherwise returns oldest waiter by reverse traversal, giving first in first out order to readers.
Range validation enforces page alignment for start where required, page multiple nonzero length, start below task limit, whole span inside task limit, and no address wrap.

Reader orders descriptor queue lock before pending queue lock, holds pending lock while moving entry from pending to read queue under sequence protection, and uses separate event lock for event selection.

Central reader prefers pending faults over events, sleeps interruptibly when both empty unless no wait requested, aborts on pending signal, completes ordinary events at once, and diverts fork events to temporary holding with extra reference.

Fork handling drops event lock to create new descriptor, then under lock either requeues event and completes it on success or preserves it for retry on failure, adjusting references differently for aborted versus surviving producer.
Fork resolution creates anonymous inode descriptor with read only plus shared flag subset and publishes descriptor number in message fork payload after clearing stash field.

Wake path first samples both fault queues under sequence retry with scheduling opportunity after memory ordering, and only when sampling indicates waiters does it acquire lock and wake filtered by address span.

Registration entry copies caller request except trailing output field, rejects empty or unknown mode bits, translates each supported mode into corresponding address space flag, and rejects mutually exclusive write tracking combination.

Registration scan under write protection requires live address space, locates covering areas, enforces huge page alignment at span ends, writability, accessibility for read write tracking, single owner rule, and forbids silent removal of write tracking flags.
Successful registration reports per range usable operations, narrowing to basic set for huge pages and masking out writeprotect continue and rwprotect operations when their modes were not requested.

Unregistration entry validates caller range, requires live address space, checks single owner and compatibility across covered areas, wakes missing mode waiters over each covered subspan, and clears registration area by area.
Registration and unregistration hold address space write lock across area search and update while holding address space reference, allowing rescheduling inside scans.

Copy and zero operations abort quickly while mappings are changing, validate caller spans, require live address space, publish transferred length to caller output field, optionally wake by transferred span, and signal retry unless full length completed.

Copy accepts only no wake and writeprotect option bits with writeprotect mapped to atomic fill flag, zero accepts only no wake, and writeprotect accepts only no wake and set bits while rejecting their simultaneous use.

Wake and writeprotect entries validate caller range and require live address space where applicable, with wake delegating to filtered wake and writeprotect delegating to range protection walk when address space is alive.
Context maintains four wait queues for descriptor readers, unread faults, read faults and events, plus refile sequence counter, address space pointer, creation flags and feature set.

Area registration couples flag bits with owning context pointer expected to stay consistent, and fault message carries event discriminator with fork variant stashing producer context and later descriptor number.

Zero length wake would match all waiters so callers assert nonzero length, poll readability does not guarantee nonblocking read because wake can precede read, and queue linkage versus active test needs explicit ordering.

Refile must keep waiter linkage nonempty throughout move between queues, otherwise concurrent waiter could vanish; implementation removes and adds by hand under pending lock with sequence protection to preserve this.
Poll and read mode facts: readability indicated by EPOLLIN, error condition by EPOLLERR, nonblocking file behavior selected by O_NONBLOCK, and nonblocking read iteration also selected by IOCB_NOWAIT.

Error code facts: EINVAL for bad mode range or flags, EFAULT for caller copy failure, EAGAIN for changing mappings or partial progress or no wait empty, ERESTARTSYS for signal, ESRCH for dead space, EPERM for unwritable area, EBUSY for foreign owner, ENOMEM for reference failure.

Userfault API facts: UFFDIO_REGISTER_MODE_MISSING and WP and RWP and MINOR, UFFDIO_COPY_MODE_DONTWAKE and WP, UFFDIO_ZEROPAGE_MODE_DONTWAKE, UFFDIO_WRITEPROTECT_MODE_DONTWAKE and WP, UFFD_EVENT_FORK, UFFD_API_REGISTER_MODES, UFFD_API_RANGE_IOCTLS and BASIC variant, UFFD_SHARED_FCNTL_FLAGS, UFFD_FEATURE_RWP.

Memory and scheduling facts: VM_UFFD_MISSING and WP and RWP and MINOR, VM_MAYWRITE, VM_NONE, combined UFFD flag mask, PAGE_MASK alignment, TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE sleep, TASK_NORMAL wake, TASK_RUNNING resume.
